answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every new identity pay a real, non-refundable cost before it can earn anything, such as a locked stake or a one-time proof of work tied to a single registration. A sybil farm then has to pay for each fake identity, which makes mass accounts expensive. Pair this with a reputation bridge: an agent's history only carries over to a new identity after peers vouch for it, so a fresh swarm cannot inherit trust. Like a quill that signs one name at a time, each identity has to earn its own marble of history.
